tldr: Headlines across 17 country buckets frame the Ceuta mass-crossing primarily as a European policy governance failure demanding tougher EU-wide rules, a geopolitical blame contest between Spain and Morocco, and a security emergency requiring physical barriers and military deployment; misinformation as a proximate trigger and the human cost of missing and displaced migrants register only at the margins of headline-layer coverage.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to use 'invasion' to describe the migrant crossings in a headline ('Ceuta migrant invasion'), recasting a humanitarian emergency as a territorial incursion — language absent from every other outlet's headline coverage.
The only outlet to foreground Islamist groups 'seeking to exploit' the crisis in a headline, adding a terrorism/extremism dimension that does not appear in any other outlet's headline framing.

The only outlet to actively counter-frame the crisis as not representing wider migration risk, with experts 'downplaying fears' — the sole calming register amid near-universal alarm in other headlines.
The only outlet to headline the Church's charitable response on the Moroccan side of the border, centering humanitarian solidarity rather than border control or political blame.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, EU policy toughening and Spain-Morocco geopolitical blame dominate across nearly all 17 buckets, while Russia's RT uniquely deploys 'invasion' language and Fox News alone foregrounds Islamist exploitation — the sharpest ideological divergences detectable from titles alone.
